correctness.rationale: Equation (11) of the source scheme gives the multiplier 1+z/(1−zT), hence the stated R_s for z=−s. Independently, put x=1+sT, B=1+s and m=1+s/2. For f(x)=(1−s/x)^2, the endpoint chord error is s(x−1)(x−B)(s/x+s+s/B−2)/(xB). The last bracket decreases in x and at x=1 has sign 2s²+s−2, proving strict support in the interior up to c. The error from the tangent at y is s(x−y)²[s(2x+y)−2xy]/(x²y³). The tangent through B has y=2sB/(s+2), and y−1 and y−m change sign precisely at c and d. Its affine error bracket is positive below B and vanishes at B. For s>=d the tangent at m has nonnegative bracket throughout the interval, checked at x=1 and B; at s=d the additional contact B cannot carry mass at mean m. Equality in the integrated supports forces exactly the proposed contact laws and their unique masses, including at both thresholds. Exact symbolic evaluation in x gives the three stated optimal values. IID products give the stated squared iterate expectation, including s=2 and deterministic zero initial data.
residual_risks: The one-step optimality does not require iid stages; the claimed product expectation does. The result controls scalar squared damping, not the error against the true flow, convergence order, or simultaneous damping over a spectrum.

value.rationale: The full law optimization under one prescribed moment is a natural design question for the existing randomized stage. The exact asymmetric two-point regime shows a strict advantage over midpoint damping at s=1 (7/64 versus 1/9), while the upper threshold certifies when any nontrivial randomization strictly loses. The sharp classification and unique equality cases are useful even within the scalar model.
residual_risks: The specified scalar damping objective is not a substitute for error, accuracy or stability analysis of general nonlinear or time-dependent equations.
